import Mathlib

inductive BinarySearchTree : Type
| Empty : BinarySearchTree
| Node : Int → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree → BinarySearchTree
deriving Inhabited

def view (t : BinarySearchTree) : Set Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => ∅
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r => view l ∪ view r ∪ {v}

def is_bst (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Empty => True
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v l r =>
    (∀ x ∈ view l, x < v) ∧
    is_bst l ∧
    (∀ x ∈ view r, x > v) ∧
    is_bst r

def get_left (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ l _ => some l
  | _ => none

def get_right (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option BinarySearchTree :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ _ r => some r
  | _ => none

def get_val (t : BinarySearchTree) : Option Int :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node v _ _ => some v
  | _ => none

def BinarySearchTree.is_node (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node _ _ _ => True
  | _ => False

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def zigzig_precond (t : BinarySearchTree) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_bst t ∧ 
  BinarySearchTree.is_node t ∧ 
  (match get_left t with 
   | some p => BinarySearchTree.is_node p ∧ 
               (match get_left p with 
                | some x => BinarySearchTree.is_node x 
                | none => False)
   | none => False)
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def zigzig (t : BinarySearchTree) 
    (h_precond : zigzig_precond t) : BinarySearchTree :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  -- t = G(P(X(a,b), c), d)  ==>  X(a, P(b, G(c, d)))
  match t with
  | BinarySearchTree.Node g (BinarySearchTree.Node p (BinarySearchTree.Node x a b) c) d =>
      BinarySearchTree.Node x a (BinarySearchTree.Node p b (BinarySearchTree.Node g c d))
  | other => other
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def zigzig_postcond (t : BinarySearchTree) (result : BinarySearchTree)
    (_ : zigzig_precond t) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  is_bst result ∧
  view result = view t ∧
  -- Structural properties: X (grandchild) is now root
  get_val result = get_val (get_left (get_left t).get!).get!
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem zigzig_postcond_satisfied (t : BinarySearchTree)
    (h_precond : zigzig_precond t) :
    zigzig_postcond t (zigzig t h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  cases t with
  | Empty => simp [BinarySearchTree.is_node, get_left] at h_precond
  | Node g L d =>
    cases L with
    | Empty => simp [BinarySearchTree.is_node, get_left] at h_precond
    | Node p X c =>
      cases X with
      | Empty => simp [BinarySearchTree.is_node, get_left] at h_precond
      | Node x a b =>
        have hb := h_precond.1
        simp only [is_bst] at hb
        obtain ⟨hgL, hbstL, hgd, hbstd⟩ := hb
        obtain ⟨hpX, hbstX, hpc, hbstc⟩ := hbstL
        obtain ⟨hxa, hbsta, hxb, hbstb⟩ := hbstX
        have hxp : x < p := hpX x (by simp [view])
        have hpg : p < g := hgL p (by simp [view])
        have hxg : x < g := lt_trans hxp hpg
        have hbp : ∀ y ∈ view b, y < p := by
          intro y hy; exact hpX y (by simp only [view, Set.mem_union]; exact Or.inl (Or.inr hy))
        have hcg : ∀ y ∈ view c, y < g := by
          intro y hy; exact hgL y (by simp only [view, Set.mem_union]; exact Or.inl (Or.inr hy))
        have hxc : ∀ y ∈ view c, x < y := fun y hy => lt_trans hxp (hpc y hy)
        have hpd : ∀ y ∈ view d, p < y := fun y hy => lt_trans hpg (hgd y hy)
        have hxd : ∀ y ∈ view d, x < y := fun y hy => lt_trans hxp (hpd y hy)
        refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
        · simp only [zigzig, is_bst]
          refine ⟨hxa, hbsta, ?_, ?_, hbstb, ?_, hcg, hbstc, hgd, hbstd⟩
          · intro y hy
            simp only [view, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hy
            rcases hy with ((hy | ((hy | hy) | rfl)) | rfl)
            · exact hxb y hy
            · exact hxc y hy
            · exact hxd y hy
            · exact hxg
            · exact hxp
          · exact hbp
          · intro y hy
            simp only [view, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hy
            rcases hy with ((hy | hy) | rfl)
            · exact hpc y hy
            · exact hpd y hy
            · exact hpg
        · simp only [zigzig]
          ext y
          simp only [view, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
          tauto
        · simp [zigzig, get_left, get_val]
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## What was implemented

**`zigzig` (code section)** — the genuine Zig-Zig double right rotation. For `t = G(P(X(a,b), c), d)`:

```
G                    X
└P                  / \
 └X          ==>   a   P
                      / \
                     b   G
                        / \
                       c   d
```

i.e. `Node x a (Node p b (Node g c d))`. The catch-all `| other => other` branch is a totality filler for shapes the precondition already excludes — it is never reachable under `zigzig_precond`, and the proof discharges those cases from the hypothesis rather than relying on the fallback.

**Proof** — case-splits `t` down three levels; the three degenerate shapes (`Empty` root, `Empty` left child, `Empty` left-left child) are closed by contradiction with `zigzig_precond`. The main case establishes the ordering chain `x < p < g` from the input BST invariant and then proves all three postcondition conjuncts:
- `is_bst result`: every subtree relation checked explicitly (`b > x`, `c > p > x`, `d > g > p > x`, `b < p`, `c < g`), reusing the original invariants for `a, b, c, d`.
- `view result = view t`: set extensionality plus `tauto` on the unfolded unions.
- `get_val result = get_val (get_left (get_left t).get!).get!`: both sides reduce to `some x`.

## Semantic audit

- **Structural correctness** (TASK.md item 3): X is the new root, P its right child, G P's right child — exactly the returned term, and the postcondition's `get_val` clause is proved, not sidestepped.
- **Set preservation** and **BST preservation**: both proved as stated, no weakening.
- All three named precondition components (`is_bst t`, root is a node, left child and left-left grandchild are nodes) are used or discharged; the precondition itself is unmodified.
- No `sorry`, `admit`, axioms, `partial`, `unsafe`, `Nat.find`, `Classical.choose`, or `decide` in any editable section; `auxcode` and `lemma` are empty but their markers are intact, and all four marker pairs are preserved.
- Values are `Int` throughout with only strict-order reasoning (`lt_trans`), so all-negative or mixed-sign trees behave identically — no positivity assumption anywhere.

Only `Solution.lean` was edited, and only inside the marker pairs.

- The returned tree is:
  - `Node x a (Node p b (Node g c d))`
  - This is exactly the standard Zig-Zig / double right rotation result:
    - `X` becomes root,
    - `P` becomes right child of `X`,
    - `G` becomes right child of `P`.
